messages:
incident-bot: P1 pager triggered — high error rate on /v1/generate from hosted clusters in us-west-2. Initial surge of 502/503 and container restarts. Paging @oncall
sara (infra): seeing a bunch of OOMs + CUDA illegal memory access in pod logs. stack traces reference `misaligned_address` in kernel module path. Repro rate ~1 in 200 requests, but correlated with long-context loads.
mike (runtime): captured pod log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T06:12:03Z runtime[pid:42]: cudaErrorIllegalAddress: misaligned address when reading KV cache
stack: 0x7f8a1b2c func=kv_read+0x1f0
... nv-kernel: pagewalk: invalid deviceaddr 0x7fffaabbcc
```
mike (runtime): Also `dmesg` shows repeated `GPU: Invalid device address` and a kernel oops on some nodes.
eva (oncall): taking lead. First actions: (1) identify affected nodes (2) cordon and drain if flapping (3) limit traffic by switching route to fallback model variant. @sara can you list nodes with highest crash-count?
sara (infra): quick grep shows nodes: gw-usw2-gpu-17, gw-usw2-gpu-19, gw-usw2-gpu-22. Crash counts (container restarts) in last 15m: 17: 12, 19: 9, 22: 15. nvml shows GPU driver 525.85.05 on all.
ops-bot: Incident task created: INC-2026-3241. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cuda-illegal-memory-access
mike (runtime): hypotheses: either (A) kernel driver regression triggered by large KV cache allocations + pagewalk under memory pressure, or (B) a race when streaming long sequences and eviction interacts with SMMU mappings. We recently rolled a small runtime change that changes prefetch behaviour last night.
dennis (eng-sre): @mike can you confirm if the runtime change touched memory pinning or multi-gpu eviction? If so, rollback candidate.
mike (runtime): yes, rollout id r-2026-03-14-evict-prefetch touched pinned buffer reuse. I can start a canary rollback on a subset of nodes.
eva (oncall): immediate mitigations we will try now:
  - cordon gw-usw2-gpu-17 and gw-usw2-gpu-22, drain non-critical pods
  - route 40% of traffic to quantized smaller model (fallback) to reduce KV sizes
  - enable pod-level `GPU_DISABLE_PREFETCH=true` env on affected node pool
sara (infra): cordoned 17 and 22. Draining 17 now. ETA 2m.
kai (support): customer impact: we've observed ~6 customers with intermittent 5xx, top affected customer: Acme.ai (reported timeout for embedding streaming). CS notified.
eva (oncall): rolling change: set `GPU_DISABLE_PREFETCH=true` in node pool config for usw2-gpu-pool; apply canary to gw-usw2-gpu-19 first, monitor 5m.
ops-bot: Deploy started: canary to gw-usw2-gpu-19. CI job jenkins/rollback-prefetch/145 triggered.
mike (runtime): while canary runs, capture `gdb` backtraces from crashed container cores. If we can get a consistent repro, attach to kernel oops. Also capture `kgdb` output and `cat /proc/*/nvml*` if possible.
sara (infra): uploaded core dumps to S3: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/INC-2026-3241/cores/
eva (oncall): canary reporting: after `GPU_DISABLE_PREFETCH=true` on 19, no new illegal address logs in last 7m. Pod restarts dropped to 0 on 19.
ops-bot: Canary success after 10m window. Proceeding to rollout to remaining nodes with 1m pause between nodes.
dennis (eng-sre): tentative cause: prefetch path reusing pinned pages while pagewalks evict backing pages — leads to transient invalid device addresses. Root cause likely a race in our buffer reuse logic introduced in r-2026-03-14.
mike (runtime): reproduce plan: run long-seq stress with KV size > 8GB on a single GPU and enable prefetch; monitor `cuda-memcheck` and `dmesg` for OOPS. I'll run repro in lab.
sara (infra): draining complete on 17 and 22; traffic shifted. No additional customer 5xx after rollout to all nodes and model fallback in place.
kai (support): Acme.ai confirmed degraded but functional after rolling change; they're asking for postmortem and ETA to hard fix.
eva (oncall): next steps / action items:
  - mike: create PR to revert buffer reuse change and add stricter pin/refcounts (owner: mike, PR due in 4h)
  - eng-sre (dennis + sara): widepatch nodes with `GPU_DISABLE_PREFETCH` until kernel/driver patch or code revert is validated
  - qa: create deterministic stress test in CI that exercises large KV + eviction (owner: mikelab)
  - cs (kai): send customer update and status page note (owner: kai, update in 30m)
  - postmortem owner: eva (due 3 days)
eva (oncall): handing off to dennis for overnight monitoring. If new illegal-access events spike >5/min, escalate to oncall-sre.
@dennis: you're the oncall now — please confirm.
dennis (eng-sre): taking handoff. I'll watch for regression windows and coordinate patch rollout with mike tomorrow. Setting alert threshold: 3x baseline illegal-memory events in 5m -> pager.
mike (runtime): found repro in lab with `stress-kv --size=9G --prefetch=on`. Running `cuda-memcheck` shows `misaligned address` within 30s. Reproduced reliably. This is a blocker for merging the prefetch change.
sara (infra): added temporary alert dashboard: https://console.redwood/alerts/INC-2026-3241
kai (support): customer comms: "We've mitigated an issue causing intermittent errors in the inference endpoint. We've applied a temporary mitigation and are investigating the root cause; we'll follow up with a detailed postmortem." — posted to status page.
eva (oncall): summary: mitigated via disabling prefetch and routing to fallback models, cordoned/flushed affected nodes, canary rollback validated. Root cause likely a race in prefetch/buffer reuse interacting with GPU pagewalks. No data exfiltration observed. Customer impact limited to transient 5xxs for a small set of tenants. Next immediate step: formal PR revert + CI stress test. Great work everyone :trophy:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-3241 updated to status: mitigated. Postmortem owner: eva. SLA impact: partial degradation (less than 1h of elevated errors for affected customers).
